prompts.text: Have you ever heard a song in a place so unexpected that you wanted to know how it got there?
Tell me about hearing music from another country and becoming curious about its story.
You can follow one song from the writer's first idea to everyone who hears it around the world. Which kind of song would you choose?
A song's journey between communities can be as interesting as the recording itself.
Discovering the original version of a familiar melody or finding out how a modern remix changed it?
Music sometimes becomes popular far from the place where anyone expected it to find an audience.
What song did somebody introduce you to that you'd probably never have found yourself?
A radio station plays a song in a language you've never heard. What detail would make you want to look it up?
Describe a time you heard an old song reappear in a completely different setting.
How do you think a song changes when people in different places make it part of their lives?
Which instrument has a sound you can recognise before you know what song is playing?
Tell me about seeing somebody play an instrument in person and noticing something you hadn't heard on recordings.
You could spend an afternoon watching a craftsperson build one instrument. Which would you want to see made?
The personality of an instrument often comes from the person playing it, not just the instrument itself.
Learning how a grand piano makes a sound or seeing how a traditional talking drum is tuned?
Some instruments have a way of making one note feel like an entire sentence.
What instrument would you like to understand better even if you never intended to learn it?
A friend hands you an instrument you've never seen. What would you ask before attempting a sound?
Describe a moment when an unexpected instrument became the most memorable part of a performance.
How much do you think the material an instrument is made from influences the emotions people associate with it?
Why do you think certain songs bring back a whole place rather than just one memory?
Tell me about hearing a familiar tune and remembering a detail you'd forgotten for years.
You could put one song inside a time capsule for a particular year of your life. What would it need to capture?
The emotional meaning of a song can change even when the recording stays exactly the same.
Remembering a celebration through its music or remembering a quiet moment through a particular melody?
A tune you barely noticed at the time can become the soundtrack to a memory later.
Have you ever avoided a song because it reminded you too strongly of a particular period?
You find an old playlist labelled with a date but no description. What clues would help you recall why you made it?
Describe a song that sounds different to you now because of something you've experienced since first hearing it.
Is there a music memory you're surprised you can still recall so clearly?
What makes a chorus stay in your head even when you don't particularly like the song?
Tell me about a tune you caught yourself humming without remembering where you heard it.
A songwriter asks you to identify the most memorable eight seconds of a demo. What would you listen for?
A simple musical idea can be more memorable than a complicated arrangement.
A rhythm that grabs you on the first listen or a melody that reveals itself after several listens?
Sometimes one short sound becomes a song's identity long before anybody remembers its title.
Do you find yourself remembering lyrics, melodies or rhythms most easily?
Two songs have the same tempo but make you feel completely different. What else would you compare?
Describe hearing a song once and immediately knowing you'd want to hear it again.
Have you noticed a pattern in the kinds of openings that catch your attention?
What's something a live performance can communicate that a studio recording usually doesn't?
Tell me about a musician changing a familiar song onstage in a way that surprised you.
You can hear a favourite song in three places: a small room, a theatre or a stadium. What would determine your choice?
An imperfect live performance can sometimes feel more personal than a flawless recording.
Hearing every detail through good headphones or sharing the energy of an enthusiastic live audience?
The same singer can sound like a different storyteller when the audience is close enough to hear every breath.
Have you ever discovered that the audience was part of what made a performance memorable?
A musician stops playing mid-song and lets the crowd sing. What does that change about the moment?
Describe a performance where one unplanned detail became your favourite part.
How do you decide whether a recorded performance feels intimate or distant?
What style of music do you strongly associate with a particular city or neighbourhood?
Tell me about travelling somewhere and noticing how the music around you changed.
You have to create a short playlist introducing someone to the musical personality of your hometown. Where would you begin?
A place's musical identity is shaped as much by ordinary listeners as by its biggest stars.
Learning about the clubs that influenced a music scene or the informal gatherings where musicians first experimented?
The music you hear coming from buses, cafés and celebrations can tell several different stories about the same city.
Have you noticed how a genre changes when musicians from different places put their own experiences into it?
A visitor asks why a certain rhythm is heard at celebrations in your area. Who could explain its history well?
Describe learning something about a community through the music people shared with you.
What music tradition from another place would you like to understand beyond hearing its most popular songs?
Which part of songwriting are you most curious about: the idea, the words, the melody or the arrangement?
Tell me about hearing an early version of a song and being surprised by what changed before release.
A songwriter shows you three unfinished choruses and asks which to develop. What question would help you choose?
Finding the right words for a familiar feeling can require more craft than finding a clever rhyme.
Watching a lyricist build a verse line by line or watching a producer turn a simple melody into a full arrangement?
A finished song rarely reveals all the ideas its creators decided not to use.
Have you ever paid closer attention to lyrics after finding out what inspired them?
You are allowed to ask a songwriter one question about a particular track. Would you ask about the first idea or the final change?
Describe a song whose storytelling became more interesting once you listened carefully to the verses.
What do you think makes a song feel personal without telling every detail of the writer's life?
When you hear a new song you like, do you replay it immediately or save it to revisit later?
Tell me about discovering music through a habit you didn't realise was shaping your taste.
Your music app shows you the ten songs you played most during a difficult month. What might those choices tell you?
The way someone listens to music can be as revealing as the genres they prefer.
Listening to complete albums in order or wandering through individual tracks suggested by friends?
Some people listen closely to every detail while others use the same songs to create a feeling in the background.
Is there a time of day when your music choices become noticeably different?
You lose access to recommendations for a week and must discover new music another way. What would you try?
Describe a song you only began appreciating when you listened without doing something else at the same time.
What makes you decide that an unfamiliar song deserves another listen?
What change in music technology do you think has had the biggest effect on how people discover songs?
Tell me about moving from one way of listening to music to another and noticing what you gained or lost.
You could try making a song using either a vintage four-track recorder or a modern laptop. Which would you be curious to explore?
Convenient access to millions of tracks doesn't necessarily make discovering one special song easier.
Hearing how a recording sounds before mixing or comparing the same performance on different playback systems?
The smallest production choices can become more noticeable as the equipment people listen through changes.
Have you ever heard a familiar recording on better speakers and noticed an instrument you hadn't heard before?
Someone asks why a vinyl record, a phone and a concert all make the same song feel different. How would you investigate?
Describe the first time a new way of hearing music changed your impression of a track.
What part of music-making technology would you like someone to demonstrate without using technical jargon?
When people connect through music, do you think shared taste matters more than curiosity about each other's favourites?
Tell me about a conversation that began with music and led into something unexpectedly personal.
Two people speak different languages but both love the same performance. What might help them understand each other's reaction?
Disagreeing about a song can lead to a better conversation than simply agreeing it's good.
Swapping songs that remind you of your childhood or exchanging tracks that describe your present mood?
People sometimes reveal the stories behind their lives while explaining why a song matters to them.
What's a question about somebody's musical taste that reveals more than asking for their favourite artist?
You're putting together music for a small gathering of people with very different preferences. How would you approach the first few songs?
Describe a time someone else's enthusiasm made you hear a song differently.
How can a person show interest in music they don't personally enjoy without pretending otherwise?
